Both these missions were suborbital, as were all animal flights for about a decade. The first animal to orbit Earth was Laika, a dog launched by the Soviet Union in 1957 who died in orbit. The first animals to orbit Earth and land safely were the host of animals on the Soviet Sputnik 5 mission in 1960, led by dogs Strelka and Belka. [...] Strelka and Belka at a press conference held on Aug. 22, 1960, days after their historic flight. (Image credit: Bettmann/Contributor/Getty Images)

The first animal to orbit Earth was Laika, another Soviet dog who launched in 1957. American reporters dubbed her "Muttnik" as a pun on Sputnik, which the Soviet Union had launched about a month prior and which became the first satellite to reach orbit. Laika died in orbit as a re-entry strategy could not be worked out in time for the launch. [...] Russian dogs Belka and Strelka were, with a host of companions, the first animals to orbit Earth and land safely on Aug. 19, 1960.

results.title: On this day in 1957, Laika the dog made history as the first animal to orbit Earth | Trending
results.content:
By Bhavya Sukheja

Prefer HTPrefer HTPrefer HTon Google

On November 3, 1957, a stray dog named Laika made history by becoming the first animal to orbit Earth after being launched aboard the Soviet spacecraft Sputnik 2. The 3-year-old husky-spitz mix, picked from the streets of Moscow, was selected by the Soviet space programme for her small size and calm temperament. [...] She was placed inside Sputnik 2, which carried supplies of food and oxygen, and launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan. The spacecraft was designed to keep her alive in orbit, but the technology to safely return a spacecraft from orbit had not yet been developed. [...] Laika was selected by the Soviet space programme for her small size and calm temperament. (nasa.gov)

Laika’s mission marked a significant milestone in the early days of space exploration, coming less than a month after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik 1, the world’s first artificial satellite, on October 4, 1957. However, unlike later animal space missions, Laika’s journey was never designed to bring her back to Earth.

results.title: The sad tale of the famous Soviet space dog named Laika
results.content:
On Nov. 3, 1957 — 69 years ago — a dog became famous for being the first animal to orbit the Earth. The dog’s name was Laika, which, translated from Russian, means “barker.”

The little female pooch was inside the Soviet’s Sputnik 2 for, literally, the ride of her life. One day, she was a stray on the streets of Moscow, the next she was in training alongside two other dogs selected for USSR space flights. [...] The other two dogs in the program Belka and Strelka — translation “squirrel” and “little arrow” — launched Aug. 19, 1960, aboard Sputnik 5. Some sources say they were the first animals to circumnavigate the Earth and survive. This is, perhaps, misleading. Certainly, there may have been animals, specifically, say, parrots, that can live up to 80 or so years, that survived on surface ships circumnavigating the globe long before the Soviets decided to shoot dogs into space.
